name: LAPA
summary: LAPA learns a discrete latent action vocabulary by training a VQ-VAE to explain the transition between consecutive video frames, pretrains a VLA to predict those latent actions from large-scale action-free video, then fine-tunes on a small amount of real robot data to map latents onto true actions. It reported matching or beating models pretrained on action-labelled robot data at a fraction of the pretraining cost.
innovation: Quantized latent actions inferred from frame transitions as a direct substitute for missing action labels.
The three-stage pipeline — latent action inference, latent pretraining, action fine-tuning — that has since become the standard shape of this approach.
matters: The clearest demonstration that the action-label gap is bridgeable, which is what makes human video usable as VLA pretraining at all.
The mechanism underneath GR00T N1's human-video layer and similar industrial data pyramids.
limits: Latent actions encode visible change, so they capture nothing about force or stiffness.
Quality degrades when the camera itself moves, which is exactly the egocentric case.
lineage: Genie's unsupervised latent action discovery redirected from generated worlds to robot policy pretraining.
